notes.title: Alt254 on Halloween night
notes.notes:
Hello there!

It's been a long time since the last news. Now we want to announce the event that will happen only [u][b]on October 31[/b][/u].

[h2]Achievement[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38343360/aa33a3faccd41e428582dbb3eb03a205ed775632.png[/img]

It will be [b]the only day of the year you can get this achievement[/b]! Enter the game and, either load the game or start one, you will discover some creatures that will roam every corner. But it won't be so easy to get rid of them, they are very elusive.

Good luck with the hunt!

notes.title: Speedrunner Update
notes.notes:
Good day, everyone! We’re happy to announce that we’re releasing today an important update for Alt254. To begin with, [b]the game now supports Mac and Linux! [/b]This is something we’ve been requested many times, and we really wanted to make the game available to as many people as possible. We hope you guys enjoy Alt254!

But that’s not all: we have called it the Speedrunner Update for a reason. Although it wasn’t developed strictly with that goal in mind, the open and minimalistic nature of Alt254, along with its difficulty, suit speedrunners very well. With this in mind [b]we have implemented a new Speedrun Mode, which adds a stopwatch[/b] to measure how long it takes you to beat the game… and [b]a worldwide leaderboard[/b] to compare your performance with other players! How fast can you beat Alt254? Try this new mode and find out -- and don't hesitate to [url=https://twitter.com/RenameStudio]send us [/url]your personal bests!

On top of all this, we’ve fixed several technical issues; check the patch notes below to find more details. We hope you enjoy these new features; you can send us your feedback here in the Steam forums or through Twitter. Thanks for playing Alt254!

[h2]Patch notes[/h2]

[list]
[*] Mac port
[*] Linux port
[*] Speedrun mode
[*] Fixed an issue where some features in the Pause menu could stop working after watching the credits
[*] Fixed a synching issue where the marks in the map didn’t synch with Steam Cloud
[/list]

notes.title: Accessibility Update is Here!
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone!

It’s been a while since we last spoke but we’ve had a good reason:[b] we’ve been hard at work on a new update to improve some aspects of Alt254’s gameplay [/b]as well as adding a series of quality-of-life improvements, like map annotations -- check out how cool they look: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38343360/8ed0fd1e22dddb771370dfa56ecd85c429eb23b1.jpg[/img] 

We’ve been working with one goal in mind: [b]to make the game as accessible as possible, [/b]so you can enjoy the minimalistic journey of Alt 254. So, without further ado, here’s a list of the new features that you will find in this new update, available tomorrow:

[list]
[*] [b]Map annotations:[/b] you can now put marks on the map to signal what you encounter along the way.
[*] You can check [b]what ground level you are in[/b] when the map shows up.
[*] The UI has been revamped to give you [b]visual cues[/b] when there's a secret passage nearby. We don't want to spoil the surprise -- but you'll notice when you see it! 
[*] [b]Combat has received a general overhaul[/b] to make it fairer. 
[*] Also, you will be [b]rewarded with HP[/b] when you defeat an enemy.
[*] [b]Enemies now only respawn after you die. [/b]They won’t do it when you reach a checkpoint. 
[*] A new system to evaluate the player’s needs has been implemented: now[b] the Oracle shows more coherent and useful clues.[/b]
[*] Some [b]puzzles [/b]have been tweaked. 
[*] Several [b]bugs [/b]have been fixed. 
[/list]

That’s everything so far, but stay tuned -- we've got a nice Halloween surprise in store for you! We hope you have an amazing Halloween -- and don’t forget to explore the mysterious and minimalistic world of Alt254!

notes.title: Patch #1: Easier Learning Curve
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! We've been working hard this week to bring you some of the promised improvements -- and here you have the result. We've focused on making an easier learning curve for the game, as well as on fixing several last-minute bugs. Here you have the patch notes: 

[list]
[*] Help for new players: controls screen at launch and tutorial tooltips.
[*] Map terrain modified to improve clarity in some puzzles
[*] Some of the bugs fixed:[/list]
   · Sometimes the achievements of "Offer your respects ..." were not activated
   · The player would get stuck in the maze if he was hit while knocked out
   · Some walls that had to be broken with the dash did not
   · Game crash during the final boss battle

Stay tuned, we have more ideas in mind that we will be implementing over the next few days. Thanks a lot for being there!

notes.title: Video: What is Alt254 about?
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! [b]Alt254 is an enigmatic game and figuring out how to beat its many challenges is part of the fun.[/b] However, as we told you [url=https://store.steampowered.com/newshub/app/1341720/view/2879444514414000949]yesterday[/url], we heard your feedback about the game being a bit overwhelming at first, and we are working in some tooltips to help in the early game. In the meantime, you can check out this nice video by the youtuber [b]The Scarlet Seeker, [/b] where he explains some basics of the game. Thanks to the Seeker for his feedback -- we hope you enjoy his video! 

https://www.youtube.com/embed/uiP7Qzb-BDc

notes.title: Development roadmap #1
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! First of all, thanks for all your support after our release! It's been a very exciting weekend, but as we said on release day, this is but the beginning of the road for us and Alt254. We've read and considered very carefully all the feedback we have received through social media, here in your comments and reviews, etc., and we want you to know that we are already working on some improvements for the game. Here's a quick list with the most important points: 

[b]Improve map usability:[/b] new features such as allowing players' annotations
[b]New tooltips[/b] at the beginning of the game as a sort of tutorial, to help new players 
[b]New enemy difficulty levels[/b] to improve user experience
[b]Some puzzles will be re-designed[/b]
[b]Bug fixing[/b] and balancing issues

We will be releasing these fixes within the next days and weeks, so stay tuned -- we'll post the patch notes as soon as they come. Good luck out there, ■!

notes.title: Alt254 is now available!
notes.notes:
Hello, world!

We almost can’t believe it, but release day is finally here. [b]We are Rename Studio and we are thrilled to finally be able to release to the world our debut title, Alt254.[/b] This adventure started a few years ago, when some of the studio members met at a games design master’s degree. After a few years of working for other studios, we decided to pursue our dream. We pitched the idea at a grants program here in Spain and got the second-best award, just enough to kickstart Alt254. 

It’s been a very complicated road from when we met at class to this day – full of twists, bumps, ups and downs – but we made it in the end, and today we get to press (finally!) the “Publish” button. [b]However, this is, hopefully, just the beginning of the real journey. [/b]We plan to add more content to the game, and we’re even thinking of new lands to explore and new adventures for you to live. 

As you may already know, [b]the game puts you in command of ■, a character made by a single pixel that will have to explore an island full of secrets[/b] in a journey of self-discovery. There’s one recurrent question we hear every time we pitch our project: why is the main character a single pixel? To answer this we have to go back to the “design table”. Antonio, one of the team members, asked himself: what makes a game really enjoyable? Its game mechanics? Its art style? Perhaps the narrative? Back in their first years, games were really funny although the art style wasn’t exactly sophisticated. We decided we wanted to have a go at that minimal art style. And what’s the minimum graphic unit? A pixel.

But we didn’t want to only have a pixel as the main character. We thought [b]that idea was powerful enough to make a whole game around it. That’s how we decided to show the game in a 26x21 resolution.[/b] We had to do some testing to find the perfect resolution, one that was small enough to be a challenge for us but, at the same time, gave players enough space to have a  pleasant experience while playing.   This is not just an experimental game, we want players to explore its world, uncover its secrets and have fun while doing so!

You might say that Alt254 is a minimalistic Zelda. It’s no secret that Zelda has been a source of inspiration, as well as the Souls trilogy (yeah, we know, everybody says so but we really love those games). But, unlike Zelda, we believe our game focuses more on exploration,[b] investigating the story and discovering secrets while you experiment with the game mechanics.[/b] Believe us, this game is one of a kind.

Alt254 is the result of those first design decisions. Now it’s finally in your hands; we hope that we were successful in exploring these concepts and ideas, but most of all we hope you enjoy the game. [b]If you want to help us, spread the word and leave us your honest review once you play it. [/b]Best of luck out there in the world, ■!
